clue.text: The information I have about the subject is in the case

parts.note: GEN is slang for information, as in 'get the gen'
IT is the thing under discussion, the subject of a sentence
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone claims their notes on a topic are all inside a briefcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The case' is grammatical, not a container: the possessive case of nouns. 'about the subject' supplies the pronoun for the thing under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this is the possessive case, used for nouns showing ownership.

clue.text: The sort of columnist to start on a second little drink

parts.note: to go is to start, as in 'ready, steady, go'
S is the abbreviation for second
a sip is a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer begins the day with a quick tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: A tittle-tattle columnist writes about the private lives of celebrities.

clue.text: Girl takes the name of a chap

indicators.note: the girl takes on, that is adds after her, the next piece

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A woman adopts a man's surname on marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman is a man's first name, so it names a fellow.

clue.text: Fish insect out of the river — it's biting

indicators.note: the fish sits outside, around the river letter, as its container

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for river
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An angler watches a fish snap up a bug, with a sharp bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' makes the fish the outer piece around the river letter; 'it's biting' is the definition, not part of the surface's fish story.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant criticism is cutting and incisive, just as biting remarks are sharp.

clue.text: To escape the snare, goddess first takes herb

indicators.note: the goddess comes first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love
to fly is to flee or escape
a trap is a snare

explanation.surface: A goddess slips free of a hunter's trap and grabs a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the goddess escaping the snare; in the parse 'first' just puts VENUS at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnivorous plant is a herbaceous species, so it counts as a herb in the botanical sense.

clue.text: Paddy becoming moderate

explanation.surface: Someone in a rage is starting to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British slang for a fit of bad mood; as a verb it means to soften or tone down.

clue.text: It may be consumed in the tea-tent

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the word tea-tent

explanation.surface: Food may be finished off in the refreshment tent at a fete.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed has been eaten up.

clue.text: Finished exam in the duties of the clergy

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such duties, as in pastoral care

parts.note: past means over or finished
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A trainee priest has completed an exam on church duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral care is a minister's work of looking after a congregation.

clue.text: Local team in split

indicators.note: the team is placed inside the split

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A local sports club is divided by a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is someone who lives in a place, an inhabitant.

clue.text: One ranked as a Clothworker?

parts.note: the cloth part is serge, a hard-wearing twilled fabric
the worker part is an ant, the worker insect

explanation.surface: A member of a livery company of cloth workers is given a rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Clothworker' as cloth (serge) plus worker (an ant, the worker insect); the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An army NCO rank sits above corporal.

clue.text: The way a sister finds a stoppage of circulation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A nurse discovers a patient's blood flow has stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine stasis is a halt in the flow of blood or body fluids.

clue.text: Deputy stableboy can't sit here

parts.note: a stand-in is a deputy or substitute
a groom looks after horses

explanation.surface: A substitute stable lad is not allowed a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a place where there are no seats, so you cannot sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Space for spectators without seats means those there must stay on their feet.

clue.text: Patriarch was a fisherman, according to gossip

indicators.note: what people say, hearsay, signals a word spoken rather than written

parts.note: Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a biblical elder used to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham's son is one of the three Old Testament patriarchs.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker demonstrated bowl

parts.note: to sit in is to stage a protest demonstration
a wood is a bowl used in the game of bowls

explanation.surface: A carpenter showed off a bowl he had made.
explanation.walkthrough: A cabinet-maker here is a material used to make cabinets, not a craftsman. Bowls is a lawn game whose balls are called woods.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine-grained timber is prized for furniture and veneers.

clue.text: Wife also figures in dance sequence

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
and means also
a chain is a sequence or series

explanation.surface: A married woman appears in a set of dance moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular slang term for one's spouse, likening marriage to a prisoner's shackle.

clue.text: Acquainted, but can't sign love letters

indicators.note: the letters of the words that come before are to be rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Someone knows the alphabet yet cannot sign their love letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aware of or informed about something is a synonym.

clue.text: For a Reformed rabbi, he's rather down-at-heel

indicators.note: the letters are re-formed, rearranged, while the surface suggests Reform Judaism

explanation.surface: A rabbi of the Reform movement looks rather scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: More shabby means more worn and shoddy, a comparative.

clue.text: Having turned round, big car arrived outside the plant

indicators.note: arrived goes around the other piece

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the big car's letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a limo is a big car

explanation.surface: A large car turns round and pulls up beside a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having turned round' reverses the big car, and 'outside' puts the word for arrived around the result. 'Plant' looks industrial but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: This daisy-like herb is used to make a soothing tea.

clue.text: Deep feelings for head of small town in Herts expressed

indicators.note: the head letter and town go inside the next piece
spoken aloud, the county abbreviation becomes a different word

parts.note: Herts is the short form of Hertfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: only the first letter of small is used

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: Someone is emotional about the head of a little town in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed' says the county abbreviation is heard as a word for loving organs; 'in' puts the head of small and the town inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tugging at the strings of the heart means stirring strong emotions.

clue.text: Make off with extremely costly woolly

parts.note: to flee is to run away

indicators.note: the outermost letters of costly are used

explanation.surface: A thief runs off with an expensive jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleecy means soft and woolly, like a sheep's coat.

clue.text: Gift without a note was previously arranged

indicators.note: the note is taken away from the gift

parts.note: a present is a gift
N is used as a note letter in crossword convention, standing for note

explanation.surface: A present was planned in advance without a card.
explanation.definitionFit: Settings arranged beforehand are set in advance.

clue.text: If there is no recipient it should return to sender

definitions.text: If there is no recipient it should return to sender

parts.words: If there is no recipient it should return to sender
parts.note: reads like a postal instruction but describes a curved throwing stick that flies back to the thrower

explanation.surface: A post office rule says undeliverable mail goes back to the sender.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian throwing stick comes back if it hits nothing.

clue.text: Result seen to be freakish outside university

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the university letter
being freakish means behaving abnormally, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Odd things are seen happening outside a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be freakish' turns SEEN into ENSE, and 'outside' wraps it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, so a verb meaning to come about.

clue.text: Lazybones riled constituents

indicators.note: the components of the word riled are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loafer annoyed the voters in his constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout or loafer avoids work.

clue.text: Most aloof when in charge that's the way

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: A manager in charge is distant, and that's how things are.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldest in manner, so the most frosty and distant.

clue.text: Old ladies cheat with bets

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them
wagers are bets

explanation.surface: Elderly women gamble and swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowagers are widows holding titles, typically elderly society women.

clue.text: Staggered from wound

explanation.surface: Someone lurches about after being hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered means swayed unsteadily; wound means wrapped thread around a spool.

clue.text: May the stone become valuable? It is

definitions.text: May the stone become valuable? It is

indicators.note: the words transform into something else, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a weight

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pebble could turn precious, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple quartz used as a gemstone, a precious stone.
